origin.description: Alias of assertArray. Returns the value when it is an array. Otherwise it stops with the check message.
origin.usage: assert_array(x, mode = NULL, any.missing = TRUE, d = NULL, min.d = NULL, max.d = NULL, null.ok = FALSE, .var.name = vname(x), add = NULL)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Value under test. A Python int is an R integer and a Python float is an R double.

arguments.name: mode
arguments.text: Storage mode of a matrix or array.

arguments.name: any.missing
arguments.text: When false, any missing value fails the check.

arguments.name: .var.name
arguments.text: Name used in the assertion message.

arguments.name: add
arguments.text: Collection that stores the message instead of stopping.

origin.details: Alias of assertArray. Returns the value when it is an array. Otherwise it stops with the check message.
origin.value: The value when the check passes. Otherwise the check stops.

translation.details: Alias of assertArray. Returns the value when it is an array. Otherwise it stops with the check message.
translation.value: The value when the check passes. Otherwise the check raises CheckError.
translation.example:

from checkmate.rtypes import NA

print(assert_array(array([1.0], (1, 1))))
